note: THE DESSERT PASS. Bakeries, patisseries, gelaterias and cake shops. Like coffee, these are SPECIALITIES not cuisines - a gelateria has no more cooking tradition to name than a coffee shop does, so cuisine stays blank unless the venue genuinely cooks to one (a Lebanese bakery is Middle Eastern and is filed that way). The gap this pass fills is structural rather than accidental: every pass so far has been organised by CUISINE or by OCCASION, and dessert is neither, so it fell through exactly as coffee did. Before this pass ran, 560 rows contained ONE genuine dessert venue. Three separate speciality values are used because they are three different searches that share almost no venues - bakery, dessert and ice-cream. Every URL came from a search result.

quotes.Pophams: The original Islington location of sceney bakery Pophams is a fine place for a pastry, sit-down lunch, and a leisurely time.
quotes.Farha: Middle Eastern-inspired bakery Farha in Leyton has it all: great pastries, great coffee, and a dining room that encourages lingering.
quotes.Onsu: Onsu is an East Asian bakery-patisserie in Soho dedicated to precision and picture-perfect sweet treats.
quotes.Suba Bakery: Suba is a tiny, West African-influenced bakery in Walthamstow that makes some of London's best croissants.
quotes.Fortitude Bakehouse: Home of bouncy beignets and sticky cinnamon rolls, Fortitude Bakehouse is a Russell Square bakery that's seriously hyped—for good reason.
quotes.Zeit Für Brot: Zeit Für Brot, an artisanal German bakery import in Islington, is home to a must-try currywurst sausage roll.
quotes.Nagare Bankside: Nagare Bankside is an achingly beautiful coffee spot with a great Japanese-inspired bakery counter.
quotes.Le Choux: A Ladbroke Grove bakery specialising in French choux buns filled with more flavour combinations than you could dream of, Le Choux is an excellent spot for takeaway desserts.
quotes.August Bakery: August Bakery, a friendly Battersea spot, makes excellent croissants, sourdough loaves, and sweet treats.
quotes.Common Breads: A Lebanese bakery in Victoria, Common Breads makes delicious and exciting traditional bakes with a twist.
quotes.Layla Bakery: A neighbourhood bakery making excellent pastries, Layla—on a corner in Ladbroke Grove—will often have a queue outside during the weekends so get there early.
quotes.Mahali Bakery: Mahali Bakery is a Battersea bakery serving inventive pastries and specialty coffee.
quotes.Kuro Bakery: Kuro Bakery is a tiny spot in Notting Hill Gate where you'll find sourdough bread, plenty of cakes, and a must-order bread and butter pudding.
quotes.Bunhead Bakery: Our advice about Bunhead Bakery? Go early and get everything at the Palestinian-inspired bakery in Herne Hill.
quotes.Tarn Bakery: Tarn Bakery isn't just one of Highgate's best bakeries, it's one of the best in London.
quotes.Quince Bakery: A tiny Islington bakery with a focus on British baking, Quince Bakery is a lovely spot to pick up buns, cookies, sandwiches, and more.
quotes.Maya's Bakehouse: We would happily select items from the counter of Maya's Bakehouse, a Tulse Hill bakery, blindfolded because there are no misses.
quotes.Eric's: Eric's is a cupboard-sized Dulwich bakery serving some of the best bread and pastries in London.
quotes.Forno: At Forno, an Italian bakery in Hackney, everywhere you look there's something that demands to be eaten.
quotes.Ararat Bread: Ararat Bread is a tiny bakery on Ridley Road that makes delicious meat or cheese topped naan flatbreads for a couple of quid or less.
